source: PLAN.md 11.6 v1 option list. This table IS the whitelist: an option may change only the JSON-pointer leaves it lists (`*` = every array element, `[key=value]` = the array elements whose field equals the value). Ranges are authored game limits, not physics data: +-20 % final drive and gear ratios, +-30 % springs/dampers/ARBs/brake force, the brake bias moves the front share by at most max_shift around the stock one (same total torque). ABS/TC/ESC are not options yet (physics has none).

options.label: Powertrain
options.help: Choose internal combustion, electric or hybrid propulsion. Conversions retain the car body and running gear; incompatible component upgrades return to stock.

options.label: Final drive
options.help: Scales the final drive ratio. Higher = quicker acceleration, lower top speed.

options.label: Gear ratios
options.help: One factor per forward gear. Every gear must stay lower than the one before it.

options.label: Clutch
options.help: Installed clutch torque capacity. Higher capacity transmits more engine torque before slipping; changes apply when driving.

options.label: Gearbox clutches
options.help: Torque capacity of the clutches inside an automatic or dual-clutch gearbox (a car with a manual clutch uses the Clutch option instead). Higher capacity transmits more engine torque before the clutches slip; changes apply when driving.

options.label: Brake force
options.help: Scales the torque of all four brakes.

options.label: Brake bias
options.help: Front share of the total brake torque; the total stays the same.

options.label: Springs front
options.help: Scales the front spring rate.

options.label: Springs rear
options.help: Scales the rear spring rate.

options.label: Dampers front
options.help: Scales front bump and rebound damping.

options.label: Dampers rear
options.help: Scales rear bump and rebound damping.

options.label: Anti-roll bar front
options.help: Scales the front anti-roll bar. Stiffer front = more understeer.

options.label: Anti-roll bar rear
options.help: Scales the rear anti-roll bar. Stiffer rear = more oversteer.

options.label: Tyres front
options.help: Any compound at any size this body's axle fitment allows (rim, width in standard steps, overall diameter). Width updates wheel geometry and inertia.

options.label: Tyres rear
options.help: Any compound at any size this body's axle fitment allows (rim, width in standard steps, overall diameter). Width updates wheel geometry and inertia.

options.label: Auto clutch
options.help: Default state of the assist.auto_clutch channel.

options.label: Auto blip
options.help: Default state of the assist.auto_blip channel (throttle blip on downshifts, upshift cut).

options.label: Automatic gearbox
options.help: Default state of the assist.auto_shift channel.

options.label: Driver assists
options.help: The car's assist electronics (physics_sim assist unit). Street offers traction control Off/On; Sport adds the Relaxed and Sport modes; Racing adds Drift and the rear-wing automation; the + ABS/ESC variants add anti-lock braking and stability control (lamps on the dash). Modern cars leave the factory with ABS and ESC, the 1990s ones with ABS only, older ones with neither; choosing a unit without them removes them. The F4 key cycles only through the modes the fitted unit offers.

parts.label: Street Assists
parts.detail: Traction control: Off, On. No wing automation.

parts.label: Sport Assists
parts.detail: Traction control: Off, On, Relaxed, Sport. No wing automation.

parts.label: Racing Assists
parts.detail: Traction control: Off, On, Relaxed, Sport, Drift. Rear-wing automation.

parts.label: Street Assists + ABS/ESC
parts.detail: Traction control: Off, On. ABS, and stability control Off/On/Sport.

parts.label: Sport Assists + ABS/ESC
parts.detail: Traction control: Off, On, Relaxed, Sport. ABS, and stability control Off/On/Sport.

parts.label: Racing Assists + ABS/ESC
parts.detail: Traction control: Off, On, Relaxed, Sport, Drift. Rear-wing automation. ABS, and stability control Off/On/Sport.

parts.label: ABS only
parts.detail: Anti-lock braking. No stability control, no traction-control unit.

parts.label: ABS + ESC
parts.detail: Anti-lock braking, and stability control Off/On/Sport. No traction-control unit.

parts.label: Electric Assists + ABS/ESC
parts.detail: Traction control: Off, On, Relaxed, Sport, Drift. ABS, and stability control Off/On/Sport.

options.label: Paint
options.help: Body colour. Visual only.

options.label: Rims
options.help: Rim colour. Visual only.

options.label: Folding top
options.help: Fit the fabric top. Shown on the model only: its weight and drag are not in the physics yet.

options.label: Rev limiter
options.help: Engine rev limit in rpm, 2000 to 20000 on a logarithmic slider. Above the stock limit the engine may leave its data range or run its pistons too fast: the setup check warns about both. Stored as a multiple of the installed engine's own limit.

options.label: Throttle response time
options.help: Time constant of the electronic throttle actuator, 20 to 100 ms. Lower responds faster; higher smooths pedal changes. Available only on engines with an electronic actuator.

options.label: Engine
options.help: Install any engine of the garage list (the shipped engines and your own). The swap derives the fuel, clutch capacity, clutch and shift points and the car's weight from the new engine; the lines under the list say what changed. The ids of the first version of this option (sedan_i4, sedan_i6) still resolve.

options.label: Fuel
options.help: The fuel in the tank, limited to the fuels the installed engine lists; the first is its reference fuel. A swap keeps the current fuel if the new engine lists it.

options.label: Gearbox
options.help: Swap the gearbox. Manual boxes (and the sequential ones) are listed; automatic and CVT follow once the physics supports them. A box is offered only if its torque rating covers the installed engine's peak torque; the car's own box is always there. The box brings its own gear ratios (the gear ratio sliders then scale them), the shift points of the auto-shift assist stay.

options.label: Drive layout
options.help: Which wheels the engine drives: front, rear or all four (with an open, viscous or locked centre differential). The new axle differentials copy the car's own (ratio and kind), so the overall gearing stays. Offered on every car whose driveline is one gearbox output into one or two axle differentials.

options.label: Front differential
options.help: The front axle's differential: open, clutch-type LSD, Torsen, viscous or locked. Offered while the front wheels are driven.

options.label: Rear differential
options.help: The rear axle's differential: open, clutch-type LSD, Torsen, viscous or locked. Offered while the rear wheels are driven.

options.label: Cylinder bore
options.help: Bores every cylinder oversize (+0.5 mm, +1.0 mm, or a re-sleeved big bore of +3.0 mm): more swept volume, so more torque and power at the same rpm. The engine file's bore changes, its maps are generated again, and the compression ratio rises because the head's combustion chamber stays as it was. A bored block takes pistons of the new diameter only: every piston grade is then sized to it and weighs more, which loads the connecting rods harder (a lower rod-limited rpm). A step that would leave too thin a wall between two cylinders is not offered; a thin wall makes the setup check warn. A turbo kit fitted to the bored engine is sized for its larger displacement. Figures in data/engines/engine_internals.json ("bore").

options.label: Turbo kit
options.help: Fit a turbo system to an engine that has none: the turbo, intercooler and wastegate are sized for the installed engine's air flow (data/engines/turbo_kits.json), the boost map is regenerated and a compression ratio above 10:1 is lowered. Boost pressure is adjusted separately in Tuning. Torque-curve engines cannot take a kit; the garage says why.

options.label: Charge piping
options.help: The pipes and couplers from the compressor through the intercooler to the throttle. A kit comes with plastic piping rated for street boost; aluminium and steel take more pressure and weigh more. The setup check warns when the boost target is above the piping's rating (data/engines/turbo_kits.json); nothing breaks yet.

options.label: Connecting rods
options.help: The rods between pistons and crankshaft. Forged steel and titanium (as in F1) survive a higher mean piston speed; titanium is also 35 % lighter. The engine's piston-speed limit is that of its WEAKEST part: rods, pistons and crankshaft. Limits and masses are in data/engines/engine_internals.json; the choice changes no engine data, only the setup check's limits and the car's mass. Nothing breaks yet (damage model to come); the setup check names the part that would fail.

options.label: Pistons
options.help: Hypereutectic and forged pistons survive a higher mean piston speed and weigh less than stock cast ones. The engine's piston-speed limit is that of its WEAKEST part: rods, pistons and crankshaft. Limits and masses are in data/engines/engine_internals.json; the choice changes no engine data, only the setup check's limits and the car's mass. Nothing breaks yet (damage model to come); the setup check names the part that would fail.

options.label: Crankshaft
options.help: Forged and billet steel cranks survive a higher mean piston speed; billet is 10 % lighter. The engine's piston-speed limit is that of its WEAKEST part: rods, pistons and crankshaft. Limits and masses are in data/engines/engine_internals.json; the choice changes no engine data, only the setup check's limits and the car's mass. Nothing breaks yet (damage model to come); the setup check names the part that would fail.

options.label: Valve springs
options.help: Stiffer springs keep the valves on the cam at higher rpm; above the springs' limit the valves float and can hit the pistons. Stock springs hold the factory limiter plus a margin. Limits and masses are in data/engines/engine_internals.json; the choice changes no engine data, only the setup check's limits and the car's mass. Nothing breaks yet (damage model to come); the setup check names the part that would fail.

options.label: Boost target
options.help: Charge-pressure target in bar, 0.1 to 30 on a logarithmic slider. Achievable boost depends on installed turbo flow, engine RPM and exhaust energy.

options.label: N2O kit
options.help: Wet injection kit for the existing bottle and nitrous plumbing. Retains the vehicle activation controls and safety interlocks. Dyno chart shows N2O off.

options.label: Driver seat
options.help: Swap the driver's seat for a lighter bucket. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Passenger seat
options.help: Swap the passenger seat for a lighter bucket, or take it out. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Rear seats
options.help: Take the rear seats out. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Audio system
options.help: Take the head unit, amplifier and speakers out. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Door trim
options.help: Thin lightweight door cards, or bare door skins. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Dashboard
options.help: A stripped dashboard: gauges and switches only, no console, glovebox or trim panels. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Sound deadening
options.help: Strip the insulation from the floor, doors and bulkhead (louder cabin, not modelled). The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Carpets
options.help: Take the carpets and boot liner out. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Spare wheel
options.help: Leave the spare wheel and jack at home. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Fasteners
options.help: Titanium bolts and aluminium brackets for the bolt-on parts. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Bonnet
options.help: An aluminium or carbon-fibre bonnet in place of the steel one. The car shows it only where its model has a separate part for it.

options.label: Radiator
options.help: Radiator grades scale the car's own radiator: frontal area, heat exchange per area and, for the race grade, the ram air coefficient (data/cooling_systems/cooling_upgrades.json). A bigger radiator lowers the steady coolant temperature when the engine burns more fuel (a turbo kit, a higher boost target, N2O). It weighs more: the part-mass tree gets a node under the cooling system.

options.label: Cooling fan
options.help: A stronger fan moves more air through the radiator when the car is slow; above about 10 m/s the ram air is faster than the fan and the fan changes nothing. It also switches on a few degrees earlier.

options.label: Oil cooler
options.help: An oil-to-air cooler adds heat rejection from the oil that grows with the speed of the air, per litre of displacement. The thermostat only regulates the coolant, so a cooler is the way to keep a hard-driven engine's oil down.

options.label: Block cooling
options.help: The engine thermal model has no water-jacket geometry, so the block is cooled by what it does have: a stronger coolant pump, more coolant in the block (slower to heat up, same steady state) and a thermostat that opens earlier. The setup check names the engine block as the part at risk when the coolant runs hotter than its limit.
